answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, slashable bond rather than its claimed identity. For example, an agent that proposes trades locks tokens; counterparties can challenge a proposal using signed receipts, and a fraud proof burns part of the bond. Spawning a nebula of fake accounts then does not multiply voting power: each account needs its own capital, and misconduct risks losing it. The yarrow and vine markets can still admit new agents, but an attacker must tie up funds and pay for every attempt.
